summary_paragraph: A woman with complex bariatric surgical history (Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with later reversal) complicated by chronic epigastric pain, gastroparesis with chronic nausea/vomiting, marginal/gastrojejunal ulcer history, and seizure disorder was admitted after a witnessed syncopal episode with dizziness in the setting of markedly poor oral intake following recent hiatal hernia surgery. Evaluation including CT/CTA head and neck, MRI brain, and EEG monitoring showed no acute intracranial process or seizures, and abdominal CT showed no obstruction or acute intra-abdominal process; orthostatic vitals supported hypovolemia/orthostatic syncope. Ongoing burning epigastric pain, nausea/vomiting, and malnutrition were managed with IV fluids, antiemetics, promotility therapy, and escalation of acid suppression (pantoprazole) plus sucralfate. EGD demonstrated an anastomotic narrowing with gastric irritation, and the narrowing was balloon dilated. Due to persistent inability to meet nutritional needs by mouth, a post-pyloric dobhoff feeding tube was placed endoscopically and tube feeds were initiated and tolerated, with plans to continue at home with services; outpatient follow-up was arranged with GI, primary care, bariatric surgery, neurology (including consideration of further seizure characterization), and evaluation for vertigo/autonomic dysfunction.
problems: Gastrojejunal ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without hemorrhage or perforation
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
